newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Malan set to announce minimum wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan set to announce minimum wage hike.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan is scheduled to announce later Friday a roughly seven percent increase in the value of the country's minimum wage from May 1, a ministry spokesman said.
"(The minimum wage) should rise to about 120 reais ($112.92)," the spokesman said.
Brazil's monthly minimum salary is currently 112 reais.
Malan was due to meet with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso before formally announcing the proposed increase in a television and radio broadcast at 2000 local/2300 GMT, the spokesman said.

The rise is less than annual inflation, which came in at just over 10 percent in 1996, but could not be higher because of the impact on the social security system and on many states and municipalities which are nearly bankrupt, he said.
